insights.claim: Nationally the two-party margin shifted 2.32 points toward Democrats from 2016 to 2020.
insights.method_note: Vote-weighted two-party margin over covered ZCTAs; fractional disaggregated votes.

insights.claim: The most-deprived ADI tenth averages 5.3 points more Republican than the least-deprived tenth.
insights.method_note: Population-weighted ADI national-rank decile means; ecological, not causal.

insights.claim: Across ZCTAs, 2016-20 swing is most associated with college graduates (Spearman rho=0.46, n=30,223).
insights.method_note: Spearman rank correlation; place-level association only.

insights.claim: Biggest shift toward Democrats: 95511 (Humboldt County, CA) at +52.7 points; biggest shift toward republicans: 78595 (Hidalgo County, TX) at -68.8.
insights.method_note: Extreme ZCTA values among places with at least 250 residents.

insights.claim: About 2 million people live in landslide ZCTAs (absolute swing of 30+ points).
insights.method_note: Population in ZCTAs where the absolute value is 30 points or more.
